Subject: OrbitAI Dedicated GPU SKU tailoring — hybrid H100/A100/L4 recommendations & next steps

Hi Ari,

Thanks for the extra context on model sizes and the expected traffic pattern — this is really helpful. Attached is a short walkthrough + cost estimate that maps three practical SKU choices to the workload characteristics you shared. TL;DR: given OrbitAI's mix of heavy long-context inference (32k tokens) for a portion of traffic and standard short-turn query traffic for the rest, we recommend a hybrid SKU strategy rather than an all-H100 or all-L4 approach.

Summary of options (see attached deck for more detail):

1) H100-heavy (memory-first):
- Best for 80+ GB VRAM models and single-replica long-context workloads (minimal model sharding).
- Pros: fewer replicas, lower tail-latency for long runs.
- Cons: highest $/hour.

2) A100-balanced (throughput + cost):
- Good middle ground for most 40–80 GB working set models where we can shard or use KV-tiling for large contexts.
- Pros: predictable throughput, lower cost than H100 per slot.
- Cons: may need more careful orchestration for 32k contexts.

3) L4-cost optimized (lightweight/embedding + burst):
- Excellent for embeddings, short-turn inference, and other non-memory-bound paths.
- Pros: lowest $/slot; high concurrency for cheap workloads.
- Cons: not suitable for your largest fine-tuned model unless aggressively quantized.

Recommended initial fleet mix for a staged Dedicated roll:
- Pilot (first 4–8 weeks): 6 slots total — 2x H100 (for canonical long-context service), 3x A100 (main inference traffic), 1x L4 (embeddings & low-latency fallthrough).
- Steady state: flexible slots scaled to committed throughput; a nominal floor of H100 capacity to cover peak long-context traffic and failover.

Operational patterns and fallbacks we propose:
- Route by model/tag: long-context model -> H100 pool; general model -> A100 pool; embeddings -> L4.
- Auto-failover: if H100 capacity is saturated, requests can degrade to A100 with quantized variant + reduced context (configurable).
- Cache & prefix KV: enable prefix caching for common prompts to reduce re-computation on A100.

Action items for OrbitAI (quick list):
- Confirm the 90th-percentile concurrent active long-context requests (estimate in deck).
- Share a representative request/response trace + a sample prompt set for eval runs.
- Approve pilot slot mix and budget guardrails.

I've attached a short cost worksheet that models TCO across three fleet mixes and a simple pilot timeline. If you're available today or tomorrow I'd like to run a 30-minute walkthrough and lock the pilot parameters.

Attachments: orbitai_sku_walkthrough_20261107.pdf (walkthrough), orbitai_cost_estimate_20261107.xlsx (cost model)

Thanks Karthik — nice crisp framing. A few engineering/ops notes from my side after skimming the attachment: 

- Memory-bound callers: If OrbitAI's fine-tuned model truly needs ~80GB+ VRAM per replica, H100 is the simplest path. But point out to the customer that we can often reduce VRAM via FP8 quantization + custom kernel selection; that allows A100 to host more of those models with modest perf delta. Call this out as a "quantize-and-fallback" plan.

- Sharding/tiling tradeoffs: For 32k contexts we should recommend a KV-tiling strategy that keeps active KV in H100 for hot traces and uses A100 for colder or sharded work. Dev — can you sketch what the tile-size and serialization overhead looks like in our runtime (ballpark ms per extra tile)? I want a number we can quote in the pilot SLAs.

- SLOs & buffer: Recommend a minimum buffer of 20% H100 headroom for scheduled spikes (training syncs, end-of-day batch runs). If OrbitAI is strict on budget we can encode this buffer as a burst policy rather than reserved slots.

- Cost sanity check: The attached estimate assumes regional pricing in us-central. If OrbitAI wants a multi-region DR runbook we'll need a separate cross-region replication cost estimate.

I'm happy to join a walkthough and surface the tradeoffs live.

—Marissa
Senior Solutions, Redwood Inference

Karthik / Marissa,

Appreciate the clear options and the worksheet. A few constraints from our side that should shape the pilot: 

1) Cost cap: we have a hard infra budget cap for Q1 that constrains sustained H100 spend. We can tolerate short bursts but not a full all-H100 steady state.

2) Model requirement: our main production model (finetuned) currently requires ~85GB VRAM unquantized and has been validated on H100. We are open to quantization experiments but need to know the expected quality delta (ROUGE / qualitative LL evals) before we move away from H100 for that model.

3) Long-context SLA: we need 95th percentile tail latency under 2.5s for the long-context pathway for 75% of requests — can the hybrid plan meet that with routing?

4) Pilot ask: start with a 2-week canary that mirrors 10% production traffic and a rollout plan that includes rollback thresholds (error rate, latency, model-perf drop).

If you can call out a concrete pilot configuration (slot counts, regional placement, expected $/hr burn for the two-week canary) I can fast-track internal approval. Also looped in Maya (CTO) for any architecture questions.

Thanks,

Hi Ari / Maya — thanks for the clarity and the guardrails. Quick response with a concrete pilot config and what to expect: 

Proposed 10%-traffic canary (2 weeks):
- Slots: 2x H100 (primary long-context host), 4x A100 (main inference pool), 2x L4 (embeddings + fallthrough).
- Placement: single us-central region (matches your fleet today).
- Expected cost (estimated): ~$9,800 total for 2-week canary (includes reserved slot time + modest burst buffer). Detailed workbook attached (orbitai_cost_estimate_20261107.xlsx).
- Rollout & rollback thresholds: rollback if 95th p latency > 3.0s for long-context route OR model quality delta > 1.5% measured by our evaluation harness on your holdout prompts.
- Observability: we'll enable token-level cost breakdowns and per-route latency dashboards; we can provision an eval webhook to collect quality metrics during the canary.

Operational notes:
- Quantization testbed: schedule a parallel quantization experiment on A100 with your fine-tuned model (FP8 trial) — if quality delta is <1% we can increase A100 coverage and shrink H100 footing.
- Autoscaling: we recommend a conservative autoscale lower bound on H100 slots to protect the long-context SLA, with burst capacity from the A100 pool if needed.
- Security/compliance: we will use Private Dedicated controls in your VPC for the pilot; SOC2 artifacts can be provided on request.

Next steps:
1) Internal approval from OrbitAI (budget ok?)
2) Sign pilot SOW (I'll route a DocuSign with the two-week pilot scope + rollback clauses)
3) Kickoff call — 30 minutes: ops runbook + dashboards + quantization experiment owners.

I'll attach a short one-pager for the pilot configuration to the HubSpot deal and route the SOW link to your inbox once you confirm.
